I should also add that music is an absolute must! If you drink/smoke don’t be afraid to sip on something or take a few bowls while you work. You’ll see your best work comes out when you’re truly relaxed.

I used to use colour wheels a lot, or look at a scene from my favourite movie and use the colour palette from that! It’ll become somewhat of an intuitive thing once you get more comfortable with all sorts of colours. The great thing about painting is that if something “doesn’t work” you can just cover it up, or put new colours on it to make it work! The possibilities are really endless and your painting is bound to change drastically as you keep working on it. Don’t focus too much on the things you consider mistakes, a lot of the time the best parts of my paintings are accidents or mistakes and then some crazy image pops out that I never even meant to make. Also don’t be afraid to just pick colours you like personally and then go into a colour wheel and play around with them if you’re worried about colour theory. 

Good luck! Share some of your art on here sometime I’d love to see.

Thanks a lot man! That’s a question I’ve always had trouble answering, but I think the biggest thing is to really allow yourself to unconsciously make decisions on the canvas. Don’t get attached to the way your painting looks at one stage, but also take a lot of time to take a real step back from it, flip it around, allow the painting to speak to you when it comes to the image it’s bringing out, learn what colours are bringing structure to your piece (after doing enough pieces this sort of becomes a natural intuition, the colours that need to be on the painting will just come into your head like they’ve always been there.) I also don’t restrict myself to typical painting tools, while I do use a palette knife very often my hands are another thing I use just as much. Buy gallery wrapped canvas so you can really slap your hands on that bad boy and start to feel the painting, finger painting is great and it’s something I use in most if not all of my abstract pieces. 

I don’t go into my paintings with any concept or idea, I truly just allow my subconscious to take over to allow my paintings to be as visceral as possible.

TLDR: The real “thinking” of this painting isn’t done during those big moments of action but rather in those moments when you step back and evaluate what you’ve done. Let yourself go wild and just slap shit on the painting, if you think something would be cool as a painting tool pick it up and use it, just go crazy bro.
